A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same verifier-learning research. All 22 pages of v1 and 26 pages of v2, including Appendices A–C, are readable and support comparison despite the revised title and renumbered results.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical bounds, proofs, and illustrative mathematical constructions, including in its appendices. It contains no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical. Its new summary table and computational-separation example report mathematical results, while empirical findings mentioned in related work are attributed to other papers.

M1.justification: Prefix-by-prefix verification, ERM-based learning, gold-trace negative-example construction, Algorithm 1, and the online learners in Example B.5 are retained. The revised soundness definitions and proofs do not introduce a different learning or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version trains or evaluates on datasets or empirical tasks. The added planning and puzzle illustrations and USAT construction are conceptual or theoretical examples, not additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against the proposed learners. Additional citations to verification and generation methods in v2 do not constitute evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, metrics, budgets, model configurations, or testing procedures. Changes to mathematical learning guarantees are theoretical changes rather than evaluation-protocol revisions.

E4.justification: No experimental ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness evaluations, or error analyses are added or removed. Appendix B retains its mathematical examples; the added puzzle illustration is explanatory and the USAT separation is theoretical.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical uncertainty estimates, or significance tests. Confidence parameters and probability bounds occur within theoretical proofs, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Neither version contains experimental scores or qualitative evaluation outcomes. New Table 1 summarizes existing theoretical sample-complexity rates; the new separation argument and revised proofs are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v2 Definition 4.1 explicitly defines acceptance through all prefixes and separates stepwise from overall soundness, with corresponding revisions to TVPAC definitions and guarantees. The proof of v1 Theorem 4.7, now Theorem 4.9, replaces an unjustified independence step with a union bound over verifier subsets. Remark 4.6 restricts generation–verification equivalence to small alphabets, and new Remark 4.7 establishes a USAT-based computational separation assuming RP differs from NP.

C1.justification: The four principal contributions and sample-complexity conclusions remain. v2 explicitly adds a computational-separation claim in Section 1.2 and frames the abstract around sequential reasoning including CoT, modestly extending the stated contribution framing.

C2.justification: v1 presents trustable verification as guiding generation; v2 restricts this interpretation to stepwise soundness and small alphabets, explaining why it fails for overall soundness or large alphabets. New Remarks 2.1 and 4.2 clarify that acceptance need not establish proof completion and distinguish the guarantees from formal-logical soundness and completeness. These qualifications materially change the interpretation of central guarantees.

D1.justification: Both versions document abstract mathematical procedures. v2 adds no implementation package, hyperparameter or hardware specification, training-time measurement, data-processing recipe, or code/data-access information.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 substantially expands positioning through new discussions of interactive provers and exact learning, plus connections to planning, imitation learning, selective classification, robustly reliable learning, and strategic improvements. These additions explain relationships to several research directions beyond those covered in v1.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title, polishes language, adds explanatory remarks and acknowledgments, and introduces the existing SVPAC loss before Definition 3.1 instead of first inside a proof. The main section sequence and Appendix A–C organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 1 comparing training data, algorithms, and theoretical sample complexities across verification goals. This consolidates material already present in v1. The single-column layout and Algorithm 1 display remain, with local pagination and spacing changes.

improvement.justification: Replacing the unjustified independence-based argument in v1 Theorem 4.7 with the subset union bound in v2 Theorem 4.9 repairs support for a central sample-complexity guarantee. The soundness distinctions and restricted generation–verification equivalence also reduce substantive ambiguity and overstatement. Together these changes substantially strengthen the mathematical reliability and precision of this theoretical paper.
